newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentina's Telefonica fined for not billing.
newsitem.headline: Argentina's Telefonica fined for not billing.

text.p: Telefonica de Argentina has been fined $40,000 a day, backdated to early March, for not billing its customers because of a dispute over new telephone tariffs, a company official said Tuesday.

The Telefonica official, who asked not to be named, was unable to give further details immediately, but state-run news agency Telam reported that the company planned to appeal the fine, which it said could total about $5 million so far.

Local news agencies said Federal Judge Liliana Heiland had fined Telefonica for disobeying her order to bill clients, which it stopped doing months ago pending a Supreme Court ruling on a new tariff structure.

Telefonica and Telecom de Argentina tried to overhaul their rate structure after the government gave them authorization to do so in a decree in late January. They raised local rates but made big cuts in long-distance calls.

However the changes provoked several conflicting court actions, including one lodged by the ombudsman and a federal court ruling that the rates cannot be applied until the Supreme Court rules whether they are legal.
The Supreme Court has still not announced its ruling.
Cabinet Chief Jorge Rodriguez told the two companies back in April that they should continue charging at the new tariff structure rates "until the Supreme Court makes a ruling."
